report_name: Microsoft's Record September Patch Tuesday Fixes 974 Flaws, Two Zero-Days

attack_patterns.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
attack_patterns.description: Used to exploit the actively exploited zero-day vulnerabilities CVE-2026-81963 and CVE-2026-85880 to gain SYSTEM-level access on a compromised machine.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-81963
vulnerabilities.description: An actively exploited elevation of privilege vulnerability in the Windows Update Stack. The flaw, described as an improper link resolution, allows a local attacker to escalate privileges to SYSTEM. It has been added to CISA's KEV catalog.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-85880
vulnerabilities.description: An actively exploited heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the Windows Advanced Local Procedure Call (ALPC). It allows an attacker with code execution to escape a sandbox and execute code with SYSTEM privileges. It has been added to CISA's KEV catalog.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-69730
vulnerabilities.description: A critical, potentially wormable remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in the Windows DNS Server. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this by sending a specially crafted packet to a vulnerable server.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-69525
vulnerabilities.description: A critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in Remote Desktop Services, often used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-69603
vulnerabilities.description: A critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in Windows Hyper-V that could allow an attacker in a guest virtual machine to execute code on the host operating system.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-80083
vulnerabilities.description: A critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in Windows Hyper-V that could allow an attacker in a guest virtual machine to execute code on the host operating system.

indicators.name: Suspicious Child Process of svchost.exe
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Child Process of svchost.exe for Update Stack
id: 26f5a31b-8b1a-4e9c-9f8d-7a1b2c3d4e5f
status: experimental
description: 'Monitors for unusual child processes spawned by svchost.exe, which could indicate exploitation of the Windows Update Stack vulnerability (CVE-2026-81963).'
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-09
references:
  - https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/patch-tuesday-analysis-september-2026/
tags:
  - attack.t1068
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\svchost.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\conhost.exe'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate system activity may spawn these processes from svchost.exe. Requires tuning.
indicators.description: Detects unusual child processes spawned by svchost.exe, which could indicate exploitation of CVE-2026-81963 in the Windows Update Stack.

indicators.name: Suspicious Parent of conhost.exe
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Parent Process of conhost.exe for ALPC Exploit
id: 8d9e0f1a-2b3c-4d5e-8f9a-0b1c2d3e4f5a
status: experimental
description: 'Looks for conhost.exe spawning from unexpected parent processes, especially those running in sandboxed environments, which might indicate an ALPC exploit (CVE-2026-85880) attempting a sandbox escape.'
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-09
references:
  - https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/patch-tuesday-analysis-september-2026/
tags:
  - attack.t1068
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\conhost.exe'
  filter:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\csrss.exe'
      - '\smss.exe'
      - '\wininit.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter
falsepositives:
  - Some third-party applications may legitimately spawn conhost.exe from unusual parents.
indicators.description: Detects conhost.exe spawning from unexpected parent processes, which could indicate exploitation of the ALPC vulnerability CVE-2026-85880.

indicators.name: Anomalous DNS Server Traffic
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Windows DNS Server Crash
id: 3c4d5e6f-7a8b-4c9d-a1b2-c3d4e5f6a7b8
status: experimental
description: 'Monitors for crashes or unexpected termination of the Windows DNS Server service (dns.exe), which could indicate exploit attempts against CVE-2026-69730.'
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-09
references:
  - https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/patch-tuesday-analysis-september-2026/
tags:
  - attack.t1499
level: high
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: system
detection:
  selection:
    Provider_Name: 'Service Control Manager'
    EventID: 7034
    param1: 'DNS Server'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate service stops or crashes due to misconfiguration.
indicators.description: Detects crashes of the Windows DNS Server service, which could be indicative of exploitation attempts against CVE-2026-69730.

indicators.name: Post-Exploitation Discovery Commands
indicators.pattern:
title: Post-Exploitation Discovery Command Execution
id: 9a8b7c6d-5e4f-4a3b-b2c1-d0e9f8a7b6c5
status: experimental
description: 'Detects the execution of common discovery commands that often follow successful privilege escalation.'
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-09
references:
  - https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/patch-tuesday-analysis-september-2026/
tags:
  - attack.t1082
  - attack.t1033
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\whoami.exe'
      - '\systeminfo.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/all'
  filter_legit_parents:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\explorer.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit_parents
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative scripts or user activity.
indicators.description: Detects common discovery commands like `whoami /all` or `systeminfo` being run by system-level processes, which often follows successful privilege escalation.
